sermon.title: The Power of Restoration Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says sin brings correction, then teaches from Isaiah 61 and Luke 4 on the process of restoration: good tidings to the poor, beauty for ashes, the oil of joy and the garment of praise. He says God’s plan is to restore people so they become trees of righteousness who bring honor to Christ, and he shares accounts of safety in Christ.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: the message begins mid-thought; he says “a fool to the correction of the stocks” without a reference (the words are in Proverbs 7:22). At about 0:37 he lists several named public figures and says they have an incurable sexually transmitted disease, and later comments on one person’s marriage; these are his own claims, have not been verified by this site, and appear in the transcript only (some names were garbled in the captions and are marked [unclear]; spellings of the others were normalized). He says Jesus quoted Isaiah “in the book of Luke”; the words are in Luke 4:18–19 and Isaiah 61:1–3 (“beauty for ashes” is Isaiah 61:3), and Isaiah 61:4 for “they shall build the old ruins.” His reading of Ezekiel 28:25 uses wording different from the NKJV. At about 14:59 a word before “Diamond” was unclear in the captions. The caption “gorillas” was corrected to “guerrillas” and “Salvador” to El Salvador. The sermon is spoken to a live audience and includes his remarks on depression and psychology, which are his own views and not medical advice.

chunks.section_question: Does sin bring correction into our lives?
chunks.short_answer: He says “a lot of things you do in life are going to bring correction,” not just sex and alcohol: steal or run with a gang and “you’re going to wind up in jail.” He says “that’s how sin corrects you,” and that most people don’t take the correction, “they just get harder.”
chunks.text: Now here it is: “a fool to the correction of the stocks.” A lot of things you do in life are going to bring correction, not just, not just sex and alcohol. You know, you’re going to wind up in jail if you go steal. You’re going to wind up in jail, that’s the bottom line. You want to hang out with a gang, you’re going to wind up in jail, you’re going to destroy your life. Are you with me? See, that’s how sin corrects you. And the amazing thing is that most people don’t [unclear] the correction, they just get harder.

chunks.section_question: What does Deuteronomy 21:20 teach about rebellious children and their parents?
chunks.short_answer: He says the passage has parents taking a stubborn, rebellious son who “will not obey our voice” to the city officials, and tells young people that parents who are “any kind of parents at all” will draw the line and correct them. He tells parents that if they live a loose life and want their kids to do right, “they’re going to know you’re a hypocrite.”
chunks.text:
Deuteronomy 21:20: parents take their child to the city officials, the police department, and say, “Our son is stubborn, rebellious, he will not obey our voice, he’s a glutton and he’s a drunkard. Deal with him, he won’t listen to us, maybe he’ll listen to you.” In other words, young people, you start making decisions in your young life to be independent, like these wild horses. Your parents, if they’re any kind of parents at all, are going to come to a place where they draw the line and say, “No, this isn’t going to happen in this house, and you’re going to be corrected.” And if parents were smart, they’d correct it way before it came to this.

Can I hear an amen? And parents, it’s the same way. You want to live a loose life and everything else, and then want your kids to do what’s right? They’re going to know you’re a hypocrite. You’re telling me to do one thing and you’re doing another. They’re going to rebel. Your sin will correct you, it’s going to bring problems. In a lot of families, how many here live in a family where there’s dissension and division and separation in the home? Really? That’s... all you guys are lying. Maybe you don’t understand what it is yet.

chunks.section_question: Why does he warn against unsettling and dividing the church? (Acts 15:24)
chunks.short_answer: Reading Acts 15:24, he says some who left the church at Jerusalem without permission “started saying things” and caused problems, and Paul brought them back to be confronted. He says people who “split the church, divide the church” will be dealt with, and that “God can bring things to correct you.”
chunks.text:
Acts 15:24: “We have heard that some of you went out from us, have troubled you, some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls.” They were in the church there at Jerusalem, and they left without permission, went out and started saying things without permission, and it started causing problems wherever they went. And so Paul got them together and brought them right back down to the church in Jerusalem and confronted them. And folks, there’s people always want to get a hair in their nose, some kind of wind of doctrine, some kind of selfish doctrine, and split the church, divide the church, and make a mess of things and unsettle people and trouble them, and the church has to deal with it.

So if you’re a church member and you want to do unsettling things, it’s going to bring destruction to you. I, I would never advise you to say anything about God’s church. He don’t mess around. You can die early, you can get sickly. God can bring things to correct you, and let me tell you, you don’t want that. Hallelujah. And remember, we all need restoration, right? Yes. So there’s people in there that we call hypocrites. They, well, they’re there hopefully because they want to change, and if you had any maturity you’d hang in there and be a source that added to the atmosphere of their change. Can I hear an amen? That was a good statement right there.

chunks.text: Hallelujah. But when you got to stay home because there’s nothing but hypocrites in the church, and there’s some people down there that, that you’re one of those people we got to put up with. You, and they do it with words. Watch the words. And also, people want your money and they want possessions. They want you to feel sorry for them and give them things. You should always go through church leadership to give anyone anything. They are parasites that need changed. Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: What is the process of restoration in Isaiah 61 (Luke 4)?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus quoted this passage from Isaiah in Luke: He anointed me to “preach, teach, speak” good tidings to the poor, heal the brokenhearted, and proclaim liberty to the captives. He says “we preach restoration,” then “the word heals and sets free,” and “you don’t need a recovery group or a 12-step procedure,” because “the word and the Spirit will revolutionize your life.”
chunks.text:
Now, the process of restoration. Here we go. “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,” Jesus quoted this from Isaiah in the book of Luke, “for He has anointed me to preach.” What’s the word? Preach, teach, speak. “Good tidings to the poor.” What do the poor need more than money, more than food? The word. They need the word. The truth of God’s word is what they need, because it will change their life tomorrow and they won’t be poor. And beside that, it’s talking about poor spiritually, and I’m lacking spiritual stuff.

“Heal the brokenhearted, proclaim,” say the word, proclaim is just like preach, teach, speak, “liberty to the captives.” He’s preaching, speaking, proclaiming, opening a prison to those who are bound, “to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of the vengeance of our God.” This is the process of restoration. We preach restoration. We preach God’s a healer. We preach God’s a liberator. We preach God as a mender of the brokenhearted. We preach this stuff, and then the word heals and sets free. Can I hear an amen? And you don’t need a recovery group or a 12-step procedure or anything. The word and the Spirit will revolutionize your life.

chunks.short_answer: He says ashes can’t be made into anything, but God says “my restoration is so powerful” that even if you have destroyed your life and there is no sign of life in you, “I can make your life beautiful … but better than before.” He says “we don’t need psychology, we need the preaching of the word and the move of the Spirit,” and that the oil of joy means God gives joy “right where you’re at.”
chunks.text:
“To comfort and console those who mourn, to give them beauty for ashes.” Now here we go. What can we make out of ashes? Nothing. There is nothing. There, there’s nothing we can do. Now, this partly burnt piece of wood, we could use it for something, even if it was just a stake in the ground, it’s usable. But the ashes are gone. And God says, what, my restoration is so powerful, young people, listen to me, my restoration is so powerful that if you have destroyed your life and there’s not a sign of life in you, I can make your life beautiful, not just like I, not just like it was before, because you weren’t beautiful before, but better than before. I’ll make your life look like mine. Beautiful. Hallelujah.

Now, that’s our promise. We, we don’t need psychology, we need the preaching of the word and the move of the Spirit in His church. How many would like beauty for ashes? You know, maybe we’re just partly burned, but you want to be beautified back. Amen. “The oil of joy for mourning.” Oh, you had a rough home and a rough life, and oh man, your mom and dad were this and your mom and dad were that, and the neighborhood you lived in was this and the neighborhood you lived in was that, and it just depressed you and caused sorrow. God says, I’ll give you joy. I won’t even take you out of the thing, I’ll give you joy right where you’re at, then I’ll take you out. It’s easy to lead someone that can smile.

chunks.section_question: What does God give for the spirit of heaviness and depression?
chunks.short_answer: He says God offers “the garment of praise” for the spirit of heaviness. He says people can mistreat you and, “if you don’t have that power of the Holy Ghost in you you can get depressed,” and God says “I’ll come along and I’ll restore you.” He says people go to psychologists to get rid of depression, but “God has that as part of His restoration.” These are his views and not medical advice.
chunks.text: “The garment of praise, honor, for the spirit of heaviness.” See, all these people are going to psychologists and everything else trying to get rid of depression. God has that as part of His restoration. Yes, people can cause pain in your life. People can, they can mistreat you, and they can cause you, if you don’t have that oil of joy, if you don’t have that power of the Holy Ghost in you, you can get depressed, you can get cast down. God said, I’ll come along and I’ll restore you, I’ll give you praise, praise and honor for that spirit of heaviness.

chunks.section_question: What are the two purposes of becoming “trees of righteousness”? (1 Chronicles 16:29)
chunks.short_answer: He says the beauty God gives is “a righteous life,” and names two purposes: God makes you a tree of righteousness, and people see it and bring honor to God. He says you couldn’t do it on your own, and when people see God working in you, “they’re going to want it.”
chunks.text:
“And they will be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that He may be glorified.” 1 Chronicles 16:29: “Worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness.” So the beauty that He wants to give you is a righteous life, a life that’s doing what is right. And so there’s two high purposes here, all right. He wants to make you a tree of righteousness, and He wants people to see that and bring honor to God, not you. Are you out there? See, you couldn’t do it on your own, but when you came to Christ, He worked it in you, and your testimony is, “Jesus changed my life.” See, that gives honor to Christ, who then are directed to Him by the change in your life.

See, that’s the purpose. And if we don’t get changed, do they want what we got? No, they already got what we got. We got, if we haven’t been changed. But when they see God working in your life and making you a righteous person, a beautiful person, they’re going to want it, and that brings honor to Christ, because they got to come to Christ to get it, like you did. The prophets of restoration.

chunks.section_question: What does God gain from restoring us?
chunks.short_answer: He says those who are restored “bring honor to Christ and are used by Christ to restore others.” Reading that they will build the old ruins and repair the desolations, he says God gets honor and “people that are really the light of the world, that bring people to Christ just by their life.”
chunks.text: Okay, what does God profit from this? Well, simple. It goes on to say, “They shall build the old ruins,” rebuild them, restore them, “they shall raise up the former desolations, and repair the ruined cities, they will repair the desolations of many generations.” Those that get restored bring honor to Christ and are used by Christ to restore others. Now, don’t you think, church, it’s about time we thought of the full picture, the long picture, that if we can grow in God, other people will want what we got, and we can be a source to bring their life to a place of restoration? That’s the profit God gets out of it. He not only gets honor, he gets people that are really the light of the world, that bring people to Christ just by their life and the way they speak. Isn’t that beautiful?

chunks.section_question: Is God’s plan for correction always restoration? (Jeremiah 27:22)
chunks.short_answer: Reading Jeremiah 27:22, he says God put them in Babylon and dealt with them “over and over,” but “his whole plan was to what? Correct them, get them to come to their senses, and restore them back to being better than they were before.” He says this means God has “something more for me than just waiting for Jesus to come.”
chunks.text: Jeremiah 27:22: “They shall be carried to Babylon, until the day that I visit them, then I will restore them to this place.” God’s ultimate plan is to what? Restore. He corrected, he put them in Babylon, he came and he dealt with them over and over and over again, but his whole plan was to what? Correct them, get them to come to their senses, and restore them back to being better than they were before. Now that’s a great message. Message that God has something more for me than just waiting for Jesus to come.

chunks.section_question: Will God avenge those who mistreat us? (Ezekiel 28:25)
chunks.short_answer: He reads Ezekiel 28:25 about God punishing neighbors who maligned and mistreated Israel, and says the Bible tells us not to avenge, “but God will come along and … he’ll deal with it.” He says “you don’t have to punch anybody out,” just “stay calm,” though “you got to stand and confront what’s wrong.”
chunks.text:
He will also avenge us. Ezekiel 28:25: “The sovereign Lord says, when I gather the people of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered, I will show myself holy among them in the sight of the nations, and they will live in their own land which I gave to my servant Jacob, and they will live there in safety, and they will build houses and plant vineyards, and they will live in safety, when I inflict punishment on all their neighbors who maligned,” mistreated them, slandered them, criticized them, did things to hurt them, “then they will know that I am the Lord.”

You see, doesn’t the scripture say, “Vengeance is mine, saith the Lord”? And the Bible tells us not to avenge, but God will come along and, what, he’ll deal with it. See, that’s what, you don’t have to punch anybody out. You don’t have to poison anybody. You don’t have to verbally attack anybody. Just stay calm. God will get them, and let me tell you, he knows how to get them to bring them to him. We can get him, but we cause them to run from him. Man, if that’s Christianity... And don’t get me wrong, you got to stand and confront what’s wrong. Hallelujah. Avenge, pay back.

scriptures.text_nkjv: ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “When I have gathered the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, and am hallowed in them in the sight of the Gentiles, then they will dwell in their own land which I gave to My servant Jacob. And they will dwell safely there, build houses, and plant vineyards; yes, they will dwell securely, when I execute judgments on all those around them who despise them. Then they shall know that I am the LORD their God.” ’ ”
Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but rather give place to wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine, I will repay,” says the Lord.

chunks.section_question: What does he say happens to people who attack God’s church?
chunks.short_answer: He says “don’t mess around with God’s church,” and that if you are “slandering and attacking and verbally doing things to harm his church,” things will come in your life, your children’s life or your finances “to get your attention.” He says God does it “so he corrects you so you can change.”
chunks.text: And I want to tell you again, I would strongly advise you, don’t mess around with God’s church. God has some strong principles, and he will correct you. You might be able to brag and say, “I don’t commit adultery, I don’t steal, I don’t kill.” But if you are slandering and attacking and verbally doing things to harm his church, I’ll guarantee you he will deal with you, and things will come in your life, or in your children’s life, or in your finances, or something to get your attention. Why? So he corrects you so you can change. Amen. Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: How did he answer a gang leader who said he could not leave? (safety in Christ)
chunks.short_answer: He tells of a Mexican Mafia leader who wept on his lawn and said “I can’t live it.” He answered that “the Mexican Mafia is not greater than Jesus Christ,” and offered to walk through that neighborhood on a Friday night “because my Jesus will keep me safe.” This is his own account and has not been verified here.
chunks.text:
Now, young people, there is a place in God of safety like this that’s just unbelievable. I remember the Mexican Mafia leader in my area came to me one day, and he wanted to talk to me about Jesus and so forth. I mean, he was one, he, he looked like [unclear] Diamond here, only mean. Diamond’s got a great face here, but he was built like that. I mean, one sweep of his hand, my head’d be knocked off. And he had this tough countenance and tattoos, and that little Mexican Mafia tattoo that they put on there, and everything else. And I gave him the gospel. Most of you know I don’t mess around, I go straight for the jugular, I go straight for the cross.

And he’s crying, this big tough guy sitting on my lawn crying, and one of my children were there, and they’re just, I mean, they were at first scared to death for Dad, and now they’re going, here’s this big gangster just weeping like a baby because of the word of God. And I’m asking him to repent and confess his sins, and he’s crying. He says, “But I can’t live it. You know, I can’t get out, the Mexican Mafia, you know, they just don’t let you go.” And I said, “Listen, the Mexican Mafia is not greater than Jesus Christ, and I’ll prove it to you. I will go to your neighborhood on Friday night, the worst day of the week, the worst time of the day, and I will walk from one end of your neighborhood to the other, and nothing will happen to me, because my Jesus will keep me safe. I said, I wouldn’t do this normally, but so you know that there’s power and safety in Christ, I will go down and do it.” Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Was he afraid preaching the gospel in El Salvador?
chunks.short_answer: He says that when communists found they were preaching, they fired into the camp from a distance, so his group had to go back through the jungle to avoid guerrillas. He says “there was not one ounce of fear in me” because “my Jesus sent me there, and he has power to keep me while I’m there.” This is his own account and has not been verified here.
chunks.text: We have a lot of things offered to us. When I was down in El Salvador and the communists found out we were there preaching the gospel, and they hate the gospel, and they would fire into the camp from a long distance of where you were preaching, because you had lanterns and stuff at night, and so we had to go back through the back jungle to try to avoid the guerrillas and being captured as Americans down there. There was not one ounce of fear in me. Why? Because my Jesus sent me there, and he has power to keep me while I’m there. Are you with me? We had to go over this terrain that’s unbelievable, there’s quite an experience, wade through rivers. We came down the road, but we had to go back the hard way.

chunks.section_question: Is forgiveness enough, or do we need restoration?
chunks.short_answer: He says “restoration is powerful and it’s offered to every one of us,” and that he still needs it. He says “I don’t want just forgiveness” and that God doesn’t want you to be “a pile of ashes” but someone “powerful,” “well groomed,” who “draws people to him” and fights the enemy.
chunks.text: And young people, you can experience this stuff. It’s not what they say on television and everything else. There is restoration in God to become like God. Is God afraid of anybody? No. Does God follow the crowd? No. Does God get depressed because people leave? No. Say it, no. Restoration is powerful and it’s offered to every one of us, and all of us need it in our life. I still need it. I get a burn spot in me, I need God to restore it. Amen. I start doing things that start decay in my life, I need God to restore. I don’t want just forgiveness. See, that’s our problem in America, is we just, “I’m forgiven.” But you’re a piece, or you’re a pile of ashes. “I’m forgiven.” Pile of ashes. No, God wants you to be something that draws people to him. He wants you to be powerful, like this Pharaoh’s horse. He wants you to be one that is well groomed, looks good, and leads people to the King, brings the presence of the King. And when there’s war, he wants you to stand up and fight the enemy and win the battles. That’s restoration, and you can have it all. It’s for you.

faqs.question: What does he say about “a fool to the correction of the stocks”?
faqs.answer: He says a lot of things you do in life will bring correction: if you steal or hang out with a gang, “you’re going to wind up in jail.” He says “that’s how sin corrects you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Immediately he went after her, as an ox goes to the slaughter, Or as a fool to the correction of the stocks,

faqs.question: What does he say about parents who live a loose life but want their kids to do right?
faqs.answer: He says children “they’re going to know you’re a hypocrite,” because “you’re telling me to do one thing and you’re doing another.” He says “they’re going to rebel.”

faqs.question: What does he say about saying things against God’s church?
faqs.answer: He says “I would never advise you to say anything about God’s church,” and warns “you can die early, you can get sickly.” He says God can bring things to correct you.

faqs.question: Why does he say to put up with hypocrites in the church?
faqs.answer: He says “we all need restoration,” and that the people we call hypocrites are there “hopefully because they want to change.” He says if you had maturity you would hang in there and be part of their change.

faqs.question: Who does he say you should go through when giving to someone?
faqs.answer: He says “you should always go through church leadership to give anyone anything,” and says people who just want your money and possessions “are parasites that need changed.”

faqs.question: What does he say the poor need more than money?
faqs.answer: He says they need “the word,” because “the truth of God’s word … will change their life tomorrow.” He also says it is talking about being poor spiritually.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon Me, Because the LORD has anointed Me To preach good tidings to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives, And the opening of the prison to those who are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, And the day of vengeance of our God; To comfort all who mourn, To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.”

faqs.question: Does he say we need a recovery group or a 12-step program?
faqs.answer: He says no: “you don’t need a recovery group or a 12-step procedure or anything, the word and the Spirit will revolutionize your life.”

faqs.question: What does he say God can do with a life that is ashes?
faqs.answer: He says “my restoration is so powerful” that if you have destroyed your life, “I can make your life beautiful,” and “better than before.” He says “I’ll make your life look like mine.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.”

faqs.question: What does he say the oil of joy means?
faqs.answer: He says even if you had a rough home and life, God says “I’ll give you joy right where you’re at, then I’ll take you out.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.”

faqs.question: Why does he say your testimony honors Christ?
faqs.answer: He says you couldn’t change on your own, but “when you came to Christ, He worked it in you,” and your testimony is “Jesus changed my life.” He says that gives honor to Christ.

faqs.question: What does he say God gets out of restoring us?
faqs.answer: He says God “not only gets honor, he gets people that are really the light of the world, that bring people to Christ just by their life and the way they speak.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And they shall rebuild the old ruins, They shall raise up the former desolations, And they shall repair the ruined cities, The desolations of many generations.

faqs.question: Does he say we should take revenge on people who hurt us?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible tells us not to avenge, but God will deal with it: “you don’t have to punch anybody out. You don’t have to poison anybody. You don’t have to verbally attack anybody. Just stay calm.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but rather give place to wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine, I will repay,” says the Lord.

faqs.question: What does he say about power and safety in Christ?
faqs.answer: He says to the gang leader, “there’s power and safety in Christ.” He says of El Salvador, “my Jesus sent me there and he has power to keep me while I’m there.” These are his accounts and have not been verified here.

faqs.question: What does he say is the problem with “I’m forgiven” in America?
faqs.answer: He says “I don’t want just forgiveness,” and that people say “I’m forgiven” but are still “a pile of ashes.” He says God wants you to be something that “draws people to him.”
